rows.verified: Workplace transport risk assessments should cover vehicle and pedestrian movements, including loading, unloading and infrequent activities.
Sites should separate pedestrian and vehicle routes wherever reasonably practicable.
One-way systems and route design should be used to reduce reversing where possible.
Clearly marked and protected crossing points should be provided where pedestrian and vehicle routes intersect.
Workplace vehicles should have suitable brakes, visibility, access arrangements and warning devices for their intended use.
Traffic routes should have adequate lighting and firm, even surfaces.
Safe areas should be provided for loading and unloading operations.
Employers should make vehicle users aware of hazards and safety precautions and monitor vehicle use.
The appropriate traffic controls depend on site layout, vehicle types, pedestrian numbers, tasks, lighting and operating conditions.
Workplace-transport evidence is site- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.

rows.source: HSE driving and riding safely for work
rows.verified: Employers must manage health and safety risks for workers who drive or ride on the road as part of work.
Journey planning should first consider whether the journey is necessary.
Routes should be selected for the vehicle type and should account for restrictions, schedules, weather and rest breaks.
Employers must assess the competence and health-and-safety capabilities of drivers and riders.
Risk assessment should consider experience, driving record, physical fitness, language barriers and vulnerable-worker status.
Vehicles used for work should be suitable for the operation, safe when selected and kept safe through maintenance.

rows.source: HSE workers who drive or ride for work
rows.verified: Workers should complete required vehicle checks and report damage or conditions that may affect safe driving.
Workers should not be pressured to complete journeys in exceptionally difficult weather conditions.

rows.source: HSE driving and riding safely for work
rows.verified: Controls depend on the driver, vehicle, route, journey duration, schedule, weather, load and work demands.

rows.source: HSE driving and riding safely for work
rows.verified: Driving-for-work evidence is journey-, vehicle- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level road-risk probability.
